units.text: # VLA-JEPA

This is the LeRobot port of **VLA-JEPA**, a Vision-Language-Action model that combines a Qwen3-VL language backbone with a self-supervised video world model (V-JEPA2) and a flow-matching DiT action head.
## Architecture Overview
VLA-JEPA has three main components:
| Component               | Module                            | Role                                                    |
| **Qwen3-VL backbone**   | ⟦0⟧                | Fuses images + language instruction into context tokens |
| **DiT-B action head**   | ⟦0⟧               | Flow-matching diffusion over the action chunk           |
| **V-JEPA2 world model** | ⟦0⟧ | Self-supervised video prediction loss (training only)   |
### Data flow
**Training:**
1. A video clip of ⟦0⟧ frames is encoded by V-JEPA2 into per-frame patch tokens.

2. The Qwen3-VL backbone processes multi-view images + the task instruction and produces a sequence of context tokens that includes special action tokens (for world model conditioning) and embodied tokens.
3. The action head receives those context tokens as cross-attention keys/values and predicts a denoised action chunk via flow matching.
4. The world model predictor uses the action tokens extracted from Qwen to predict future V-JEPA2 frame embeddings; a regression loss on those predictions is added to the action loss.

**Inference:**
Only Qwen + the action head are used. The world model is not needed at inference time.
### Action head details
Available presets via ⟦0⟧:
| Preset  | Heads | Head dim |

The preset only sets the attention geometry, and each entry can be overridden by
⟦0⟧ / ⟦1⟧. Two widths follow from it:
- the DiT's **internal** width is ⟦0⟧ (768 for ⟦1⟧), derived rather than configured;

- the DiT's **output** width, and the width of the action-decoder and state-encoder MLPs, is
  ⟦0⟧ (default 1024).
So ⟦0⟧ runs a 768-wide transformer that projects to 1024. The two are independent.
### World model details
The video predictor is a ViT-style transformer (⟦0⟧) that takes:
- **Frame tokens**: V-JEPA2 patch embeddings projected to ⟦0⟧
- **Action tokens**: Qwen action token embeddings projected to ⟦0⟧
It uses block-causal attention so each temporal step can attend to all previous steps. The predictor's input ⟦0⟧ equals ⟦1⟧ (e.g. 2 views × 1024 = 2048 for the pretrained checkpoints).
## Pretrained Checkpoints
Three checkpoints are available directly inside the LeRobot org here: [⟦0⟧](⟦1⟧), converted from [ginwind/VLA-JEPA](⟦2⟧):
| Checkpoint                    | Dataset           | Cameras                 | World model | Action dim |
| ⟦0⟧     | LIBERO-10         | 2 (agentview + wrist)   | Enabled     | 7          |
| ⟦0⟧   | DROID 1.0.1       | 2 (exterior left views) | Enabled     | 7          |
| ⟦0⟧ | OXE Bridge / RT-1 | 1 (view duplicated ×2)  | Enabled     | 7          |
All checkpoints use ⟦0⟧ as the language backbone.
## Configuration
Key parameters in ⟦0⟧:

| Parameter                    | Default       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

| ⟦0⟧                 | 7             | Number of actions predicted per inference call                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

| ⟦0⟧             | 7             | Steps executed from the predicted chunk before re-planning                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

| ⟦0⟧           | 8             | Video clip length fed to the world model                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

| ⟦0⟧         | ⟦1⟧        | Whether to load and train the V-JEPA2 predictor                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

| ⟦0⟧    | 0.1           | Weight of the JEPA prediction loss relative to the action loss                                                                                                                                                                                             |

| ⟦0⟧ | ⟦1⟧       | Encode the world-model context causally (one prefix-only V-JEPA2 pass per context position) so bidirectional attention can't leak future frames into the predictor input. Costs ⟦2⟧ extra encoder calls                                            |

| ⟦0⟧    | 4             | Euler integration steps for action denoising                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

| ⟦0⟧                | ⟦1⟧       | Freeze the Qwen3-VL backbone and only train the action head                                                                                                                                                                                                |

| ⟦0⟧             | ⟦1⟧        | Key prefixes allowed to be randomly re-initialised on load (for cross-embodiment transfer, see [Fine-tuning on a different embodiment](⟦2⟧))                                                                            |

| ⟦0⟧           | ⟦1⟧        | ⟦2⟧ every camera frame is resized to before the Qwen3-VL vision tower. ⟦3⟧ keeps the native resolution, and Qwen3-VL's patch count grows with it, so a 720x1280 camera can exhaust GPU memory. The published checkpoints use ⟦4⟧ |

| ⟦0⟧                | 6             | Index of the gripper dimension in the action vector. Ignored when ⟦1⟧ matches a dataset action name                                                                                                                                      |

| ⟦0⟧        | ⟦1⟧ | Action-dimension names identifying the gripper; the matched index wins over ⟦2⟧                                                                                                                                                                  |

| ⟦0⟧          | 0.5           | Threshold used by ⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧. Note ⟦3⟧ runs _after_ unnormalization, so this is compared against the gripper's physical value                                                                          |

| ⟦0⟧    | ⟦1⟧       | Snap the gripper dim to ⟦2⟧ before unnormalization. LIBERO-specific, see below                                                                                                                                                                          |

| ⟦0⟧    | ⟦1⟧       | Binarize the gripper dim to ⟦2⟧ after unnormalization. LIBERO-specific, see below                                                                                                                                                                      |

| ⟦0⟧    | ⟦1⟧        | Clip normalized actions to [-1, 1] before unnormalizing. Only applied when ⟦2⟧ uses ⟦3⟧; ignored (with a warning) under ⟦4⟧, where it would truncate at 1 sigma                                                                          |

| ⟦0⟧      | ⟦1⟧        | Camera views the world-model predictor is built for. Baked into checkpoint shapes. ⟦2⟧ falls back to ⟦3⟧, which is what the published checkpoints encode                                                                                |

⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ are a port of the starVLA LIBERO eval
loop and are only correct for LIBERO's action convention. ⟦2⟧ writes ⟦3⟧ into
_normalized_ space, the unnormalizer maps those to the midpoint and the max, and ⟦4⟧ then
compares that **physical** value against ⟦5⟧ (0.5). For a gripper measured in
degrees, mm or [0, 100], both values land above the threshold and the commanded gripper becomes a
constant. They default to ⟦6⟧ for that reason; enable them only for LIBERO-style setups, and
set ⟦7⟧ in the gripper's own units if you do. The processor factory warns when the
dataset stats show the range cannot work.
## Training

Number of training steps may vary based on dataset size and compute budget. The original paper pretrained for 50k on ssv2 + droid jointly, then additional 30k steps for LIBERO, but fewer steps may still yield good performance when fine-tuning from the provided pretrained checkpoints.

### Fine-tuning on a different embodiment

When the target robot has a different action or state dimensionality than the pretrained checkpoint, the input/output projection layers of the action head will have mismatched shapes and cannot be loaded directly. ⟦0⟧ lets you list the key prefixes that are allowed to mismatch — those layers are randomly re-initialised while every other weight is reused from the checkpoint. Any shape mismatch outside the listed prefixes raises an error.
The layers that depend on ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ are:
| Layer                                     | Key prefix                          |
| Action encoder (action_dim → inner_dim)   | ⟦0⟧ |
| Action decoder (hidden_size → action_dim) | ⟦0⟧ |
| State encoder (state_dim → inner_dim)     | ⟦0⟧  |
If your robot has no proprioceptive state, omit ⟦0⟧ from the list.

## Fine-tuning on datasets with a different number of cameras
The pretrained world model predictor was trained with ⟦0⟧, i.e. two camera views.

This view count used to be read from ⟦0⟧, which also names the JEPA encoder's _temporal_ tubelet size. ⟦1⟧ is the field for it now; leaving it at ⟦2⟧ falls back to ⟦3⟧ so the published checkpoints keep loading unchanged.
**Default behaviour — view padding / trimming (no action required)**
When fine-tuning from ⟦0⟧ the model automatically adjusts the number of views fed to the world model to match ⟦1⟧:
- **Single-view datasets (e.g. BridgeV2):** the single-view latent is duplicated to produce a two-view world-model input, preserving the JEPA self-supervised signal without any weight mismatch.

- **>2-view datasets (e.g. DROID with 3 views):** all views are passed to the Qwen backbone (for richer context), but only the first ⟦0⟧ views (one wrist + one third-person, following the configured view order) are used for the world model.
**Option 1 — Disable the world model**
Set ⟦0⟧ to skip the JEPA loss entirely. Only the Qwen backbone and action head are loaded and trained. This is sufficient for good action performance.
**Option 2 — Reinitialize the predictor input projection**

If you want to change ⟦0⟧ to a value other than 2, load the checkpoint with ⟦1⟧ and reinitialize ⟦2⟧ for the new ⟦3⟧. All other predictor block weights (attention, MLP, norm, output projection) are camera-count-agnostic and can be reused from the pretrained checkpoint.
